# Component affine normalization: an exact criterion and an integral lift

Historical claim of scope (pending review here): proved criterion and arithmetic refinement. The connected
counterexample itself is already archived in
`candidate e3932c47b953f7cd`; it is not a new
example. This note answers the stronger anisotropic-normalization
question and shows that the universal graph can be realized as an
EXACT integer-base set, at the cost of increased integer dimension.
It proves no sharp cap budget for that increased dimension.

Use a finite full-rank lattice-convex set P subset Z^k. The same
statements apply to a component in its intrinsic saturated affine
lattice, after the usual integer translation and lattice-basis
reduction. Let L(P) be the scalar functions preserving every anchored
convex representation in P, and Aff(P) the restrictions of ordinary
affine functions. The finite dependence components and their exact
representations are those defined in
`candidate dbf3b23d25004153`.

## 1. The exact criterion for a common continuous map and affine shear

Fix a connected dependence component P, continuous dimension d>=1,
and 0<eta<=1/|P|, so the uniform-weight family is among those tested.
Consider all actual compatible families of full-dimensional fibers
K_z in R^d, z in P, whose normalized volumes have a common positive
lower bound eta. Thus, writing M=sum_z |K_z|,

    |K_z|/M>=eta>0 for every z in P.                      (1)

The following are equivalent:

1. L(P)=Aff(P).
2. Uniformly over such families, a common invertible continuous map T
   and an ordinary base-affine shear Bz+c can make every transformed
   fiber T K_z+Bz+c lie in one fixed ball and have volume bounded
   below by one fixed positive constant. The constants may depend on
   P,d,eta, but not on the family.

The volume upper bound is automatic from the enclosing ball. The
continuous determinant is not required to equal one in this statement.

For sufficiency, normalize one anchor fiber by the maximum-inscribed
simplex map. Its normalized volume lies between kappa_d and
kappa_d[d(d+2)]^d. Equation (1) therefore gives uniform positive lower
and upper bounds for EVERY normalized fiber volume. Since the
dependence component is connected, the finite incidence shape
propagation proved in Section 3 of the cited dependence note, or the
source-target comparison in
`candidate c0cb4d49afb99df3`,
gives a common diameter bound D for all fibers. These statements bound
diameters regardless of their positions.

Here is the remaining position argument with its exact hypothesis.
Let c_z be the normalized fiber centroids. Choose a finite matrix A
whose rows are actual anchored-representation relations and whose
kernel is L(P). Such a matrix exists: for each anchor the representation
polytope has finitely many vertices, and relations at those vertices
imply all its other relations. If A has b rows, compatibility gives

    |c_j-sum_w lambda_w c_w|<=D

for each row, because both points belong to K_j. Hence

    dist(c,L(P) tensor R^d)<=sqrt(b)D/sigma,              (2)

where sigma is the smallest nonzero singular value of A. If A=0 the
distance is zero. Under L(P)=Aff(P), the projected center array is
exactly B_0 z+c_0 for an ordinary affine map on the base. Subtract it.
Equation (2) and the diameter bound place all fibers in a common ball;
translations do not change their uniformly positive volumes.

For necessity, suppose g in L(P) is not affine. There is a real affine
dependence a=(a_z), with

    sum a_z=0,   sum a_z z=0,   b:=sum a_z g(z) !=0.      (3)

For t tending to infinity, take

    K_(t,z)=t g(z)e_1+B_2^d.

All normalized weights are 1/|P|. All required compatibility inclusions
hold with equality, so this is an actual convex family over P.
Suppose common maps T_t and affine shears put these fibers in R B_2^d
and give each volume at least v>0. The common ellipsoidal shape implies

    ||T_t||<=R,
    |det T_t|>=v/kappa_d,
    sigma_min(T_t)>=v/(kappa_d R^(d-1)).                 (4)

The first inequality follows by comparing opposite points in each
image ellipsoid, independently of its center. The transformed centers
c'_(t,z) are all in the enclosing ball. Applying (3) cancels the
affine shear and translation, giving

    sum_z a_z c'_(t,z)=t b T_t e_1.

Its left side has norm at most R sum|a_z|, whereas its right side has
a positive constant times t as a lower bound by (4). This is impossible.
It proves necessity even with variable determinants, as long as the
desired normalized fibers keep a uniform positive volume.

Thus incidence connectedness controls shapes but does NOT supply the
ordinary-affine positional condition. The criterion is exactly
L(P)=Aff(P), not connectedness alone.

## 2. The archived connected obstruction already fails the criterion

For clarity, the archived support is the 13-point integer set of

    x,y,z>=0, x+z>=1,
    x+2y+z<=5, 2x+y+z<=4, 3x+2z<=6

in R^3. Its dependence hypergraph is connected. Its seven vertices are

    a=(0,0,1), b=(0,0,3), c=(0,1,3), d=(0,2,1),
    e=(1,0,0), f=(1,2,0), h=(2,0,0).

The complete integer list, all anchored face equations, and the exact
verification are in `candidate e3932c47b953f7cd`.
That calculation gives

    dim L(P)=5,   dim Aff(P)=4.

An integer-valued nonaffine mode g has g(c)=3 and
g(a)=g(b)=g(e)=g(f)=0, while

    c=b-e/2+f/2.                                        (5)

It is affine on every anchored face and hence belongs to L(P).
The family t g(p)e_1+B already has equal weights at every positive
fiber. By Section 1, even allowing arbitrary common anisotropic maps
with uniformly positive output volumes does not repair its positional
escape using an ordinary affine shear. There is just ONE dependence
component here, so simultaneous normalization of different components
is not the source of the failure.

## 3. A rational universal graph is exactly lattice-convex

There is an arithmetic strengthening of the archived universal lift.
Write ell=dim L(P), with P spanning R^k, and set s=ell-k-1>=0.
There are integer-valued functions g_1,...,g_s on P such that

    1,z_1,...,z_k,g_1,...,g_s

are a REAL basis of L(P). To prove this, all anchored representation
polytopes are rational because P is integral. The finite matrix of
their vertex relations is therefore rational, so L(P) has a rational
basis. Extend the rational independent family 1,z_1,...,z_k to such
a basis and multiply each extra basis function by a positive integer
clearing its finitely many denominators.

Define

    Phi(z)=(z,g_1(z),...,g_s(z)) in Z^(k+s),
    P_hat=Phi(P).                                       (6)

Then P_hat has full affine dimension k+s=ell-1 and satisfies

    conv(P_hat) intersect Z^(ell-1)=P_hat.               (7)

In fact a stronger assertion holds: every point of conv(P_hat) whose
FIRST k coordinates are integral already belongs to P_hat. Indeed,
write such a point as sum lambda_w Phi(w). Its projection is an
integer point z=sum lambda_w w in conv(P), hence z in P. Preservation
of that anchored representation by every g_i forces all remaining
coordinates to equal g_i(z). The point is precisely Phi(z).

Full affine dimension follows from independence of the displayed
basis functions. No extra lattice point can appear because denominators
were cleared: the first k integral coordinates and the anchored
relations already determine every added coordinate exactly.

Representations are preserved in both directions: one direction uses
the defining identities of g_i, and the other uses projection onto z.
Consequently the finite convexity spaces and their Helly numbers agree:

    h(P_hat)=h(P).                                      (8)

For example their closed traces obey
Phi(P intersect conv A)=P_hat intersect conv Phi(A), for all A subset P.
This is the same representation argument as the archived universal
lift, now with the extra feature coordinates genuinely integral.

## 4. Actual convex fibers over the lifted INTEGER base

Let R_z be any compatible residual convex fibers over P, with positive
full d-volume. Set

    C_hat=conv union_(z in P) ({Phi(z)} times R_z).

Equation (7) says the only integer bases of C_hat are Phi(P).
At each such base every lifted convex representation projects to the
same original anchored representation, so compatibility gives the
fiber EXACTLY R_z. Since Phi(P) spans R^(ell-1) and one fiber is full
dimensional, C_hat is an actual convex body in R^(ell-1) times R^d.

Suppose the original fibers have the form K_z=R_z+h(z), where every
coordinate of h belongs to L(P). Then h(z)=H(Phi(z)) for an ordinary
affine vector-valued map H. The ambient affine map

    (Z,X) -> (projection_(first k coordinates) Z, X+H(Z))

sends the lifted mixed set exactly to the original one. It preserves
fiber volume and pulls each original containing halfspace back to a
containing halfspace or to the whole source. Therefore

    depth_original(z,x+h(z))>=depth_lifted(Phi(z),x).      (9)

The residual compactification in the archived dependence note can
thus be realized with an actual standard integer lattice. This does
not make the projection map a unimodular bijection, or preserve the
original number of integer coordinates.

## 5. The exact dimension cost remains

The arithmetic lift uses ell-1 integer coordinates rather than k.
If ell>k+1, no universal affine realization making EVERY member of
L(P) ordinary-affine can have affine dimension less than ell-1:
the space of affine functions on a D-dimensional hull has dimension
D+1. This is a genuine representation-dimension requirement, not an
artifact of clearing denominators.

In the archived connected example the lift can simply be

    Phi(p)=(p,g(p)) in Z^4.

It has full rank four, is exactly lattice-convex, and preserves h(P).
The original integer rank is three. Applying only a dimension-based
bound 2^(-n)Gamma_d to this lifted problem would supply Gamma_d/16
rather than the desired original Gamma_d/8. The exact equality of
finite Helly numbers in (8), and the inherited bound h(P)<=8, do not
by themselves remove that factor: a sharp Gamma_d/h(P) theorem for
these fiber families is still an additional, unproved assertion.

The new arithmetic realization therefore preserves the integer-point
incidence data exactly, while exposing the remaining quantitative
cost. Neither ordinary affine-shear compactness of every connected
component nor a cost-free lift to a larger integer space is validly
inferred.
